intent: A button that closes its Dialog when pressed, for a close action the consumer composes inside the popup.
typical_uses: The Cancel action in a DialogFooter
The one close control when DialogContent's built-in close button is turned off

dont_use_when.situation: A top-right close button for the popup

instead.note: DialogContent renders one by default through `showCloseButton`, named by `closeLabel`.

dont_use_when.situation: An action that must keep the dialog open when it fails, such as a save the server may reject

instead.note: DialogClose closes the dialog on press unless its own `onClick` calls `event.preventBaseUIHandler()`; a Button's handler can instead close it through the root's controlled `open` once the action succeeds.

invariants.text: DialogClose renders a native button with no kit class of its own; its look comes from `className` or from the element passed through `render`.
A press closes the Dialog whose root encloses it, reporting a close press as the reason to that root's `onOpenChange`, unless its own `onClick` calls `event.preventBaseUIHandler()`.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a non-button element through `render` while `nativeButton` stays at its default
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `nativeButton={false}` together with a `render` element that is not a native button, so the primitive adds the button role and keyboard handling itself

a11y.by: the primitive's Dialog.Close renders a native button; dialog.test.tsx asserts getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }) on it and that clicking it removes the dialog ("closes via a consumer-composed DialogClose")

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the close button's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the close button's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit sets no style of its own on this button.

good.title: A Cancel action in the footer

bad.title: A close control outside any Dialog root
bad.why: The primitive's Close reads the nearest Dialog root's state through context and throws when there is none.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
